title: Decompose shared Terraform modules to isolate provider constraints and reduce state drift
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: Over the last 18 months we accumulated cross-environment Terraform modules that bake provider blocks (aws/azurerm/google) and implicit assumptions about provider versions. This has caused provider version conflicts, frequent state refresh churn, and coupling between VPC/network templates and cloud-provider-specific lifecycle logic. Goal: Split shared modules into provider-agnostic core modules and small provider-specific adapters, codify provider constraints at the workspace level, and introduce a migration path that preserves existing state with minimal downtime. Outcome: reduced plan noise, fewer `terraform init`/provider upgrade incidents, and clearer module ownership for multi-cloud proofs-of-concept.
acceptance_criteria: Core networking module (network-core) contains only resource-agnostic inputs/outputs and no provider blocks
Provider adapters (aws-network-adapter, azurerm-network-adapter) hold provider blocks and provider-specific resources
All existing workspaces successfully migrated with state import where necessary and no accidental resource recreation
CI passes for all affected repo pipelines; rollbacks documented
Documentation updated: Confluence how-to, example workspace configs, and upgrade checklist
technical_notes: Approach: replace monolithic modules with two-layer pattern: module://network-core + module://{cloud}-adapter

Provider pinning: specify required_providers in root workspace with explicit version constraints (e.g. aws = "~> 4.70" -> plan for 5.x later) and move provider installation to workspace-level providers.tf
Use provider aliasing for multi-account setups (provider "aws" alias = "management") and pass provider aliases down to adapters via variables
State handling: create state migration scripts using `terraform state mv` + `terraform import` where resource addresses change; store migration steps in repo as idempotent bash scripts
Terragrunt: update include/hcl to inject provider_version var and avoid hardcoding; keep legacy wrappers for two cycles
Testing: create a sandbox AWS workspace per region to run full apply and drift detection before promoting to staging
Compatibility: keep backwards-compatible module inputs for 1 cycle (deprecate via warning in provider-adapter outputs)
migration_plan: 1) Audit: run `terraform providers` across all workspaces and record provider versions + state addresses (scripted).
2) Create `network-core` module and `aws-network-adapter` module in infra-modules repo; implement shim to accept old inputs.
3) Add workspace-level providers.tf to each workspace with required_providers and provider aliases; create PRs per workspace starting with low-risk infra (dev -> staging -> prod).
4) Run `terraform plan` in CI for each PR; if address changes, author a migration script and attach to PR.
5) Execute migration during maintenance window: apply adapter changes, run state migrations, verify resources unaffected.
6) Monitor for 72 hours using metric dashboards (apply times, drift reports) and rollback if unexpected deletions appear.
7) After 2 successful cycles, remove legacy monolithic modules and update documentation and examples.
rollout_and_risks: Risk: accidental resource recreation due to address changes. Mitigation: thorough state-diff and explicit `terraform state mv` scripts reviewed in PRs.

Risk: provider upgrade incompatibilities (e.g., aws provider v5 behavior changes). Mitigation: pin to safe minor version, run Terraform 1.5 TFE-compatible builds, and test provider upgrade in sandbox workspace.
Risk: prolonged maintenance window for larger workspaces. Mitigation: schedule per-team windows and do adapters incrementally.
Rollback: keep previous state snapshots and provide `restore_state.sh` that can re-point backend and reapply previous module layout.
